Khoekhoe

[edit]

[edit]

A loanword from an extinct, Sog- Eastern Sudanic language, where it referred to pennisetum; compare Ik rébè (“pennisetum”) and Luo bél (“sorghum”).[1]

Noun

[edit]

pere ? (dual, plural)

  1. grain, bread

Etymology 3

[edit]

From Old French per and Anglo-Norman peir, from Latin pār.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • per, peer, peere, pier, pyer, piere, pyere, pir

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /peːr/

Noun

[edit]

pere (plural peres)

  2. A peer; one who is equal to or like another.
  3. A rival, enemy, or competitor; one who is in opposition.
  4. An individual who is of the same social class or standing as another.
  5. An associate or collaborator; one who works or associates with another.
  6. A member of the nobility or ruling class of a country or settlement.
  7. (anatomy, rare) A body part connected or concomitant with another.
Related terms
[edit]
  • dosse per
  • noumpere
  • parage
  • pereles
Descendants
[edit]
  • English: peer
  • Scots: peer
References
[edit]
  • “pẹ̄r, n.”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 21 April 2019.

Adjective

[edit]

pere

  1. The same; having no differences from something else.
References
[edit]
  • “pẹ̄r, adj.”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 21 April 2019.

[edit]
  • Hallap, V.; Adler, E.; Grünberg, S.; Leppik, M. (2012), “pere”, in Vadja keele sõnaraamat [A dictionary of the Votic language]‎[7], 2nd edition, Tallinn

Walloon

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French pere, pedre, from Latin pater, patrem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɛːʀ/

Noun

[edit]

pere m (plural peres)

  1. father

Yoruba

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • پعِرعِ

Etymology

[edit]

Adverb sense derives from ideophone sense

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /k͡pé.ɾé/, /k͡pè.ɾé/

Ideophone

[edit]

péré or pèré

  1. (of an object) being luxuriant or lush
  2. (of an object) being only some amount or quantity

Adverb

[edit]

péré

  1. only
    ẹyọ mẹ́ta péré ― Only three entities

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Only used with numbers

Related terms

[edit]
  • nìkan

Zazaki

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Persian پاره (pâre).

Noun

[edit]

pere (pâre)

  1. money
